title: Quadratic equations, inequalities and the discriminant

points.text: Solving quadratic equations by factorising, completing the square or the formula
Discriminant and the nature of the roots

bigPicture: Quadratic equations have up to two real roots; the discriminant tells you how many without solving. Inequalities need a sketch, not just roots.

keyIdeas.cue: Three ways to solve ax² + bx + c = 0?
keyIdeas.answer: Factorise, complete the square, or the quadratic formula.

keyIdeas.cue: How do you solve x² − x − 6 > 0?
keyIdeas.answer: Find roots (−2, 3), sketch: positive outside the roots → x < −2 or x > 3.

keyIdeas.cue: What does Δ = b² − 4ac tell you?
keyIdeas.answer: Δ > 0: two distinct real roots; Δ = 0: one repeated root; Δ < 0: no real roots.

keyTerms.def: graph touches the x-axis at its vertex

workedExamples.title: Parameter
workedExamples.prompt: Find k such that x² + kx + 4 = 0 has no real roots.

misconceptions.right: Δ = 0 gives one repeated root; 'real roots' means Δ ≥ 0.

practice.prompt: Find the values of m for which the line y = mx − 1 is tangent to y = x² + 3.

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.

formulaBooklet.note: 'Given' = appears in the SL or prior-learning sections of the official AA formula booklet (2021 edition), which is provided in both papers. The ISL one-page sheet (Jan 2026) is a third-party summary of the same SL formulas; use the official booklet in the exam. 'Memorise' = needed but not printed.
